lines.text: The men of Ephraim contend with Gideon for not calling them, and their anger subsides when he credits them.
Gideon crosses the Jordan, but Succoth and Penuel refuse his exhausted troops bread, and he threatens both towns.
Gideon surprises the army at Karkor, and he captures the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna.
Gideon returns by the Ascent of Heres, disciplines Succoth with thorns and briers, and pulls down the tower of Penuel.
Gideon says the men killed at Tabor were his brothers, and Jether, his firstborn, draws his sword against the kings.
